title: Onprem init ops cheatsheet & Terraform pragmatics
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic runbook and collection of operational heuristics for first-time bootstrapping, horizontal scale experiments, and operator/instance rotations for private control plane installs (VPC and on-prem).

Audience:
- Field SREs and deployment engineers running customer onprem installs
- Solutions engineers validating cutovers
- Terraform authors implementing secure, idempotent module wiring

Notes on scope and tone:
- This is intentionally terse — checklist-first, then deeper rationale and example TF snippets.
content_addendum:
PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS (must pass before you apply):
- Network: confirm CIDR non-overlap with customer network, confirm egress policy to Redwood control endpoints (if used), or ensure control plane has outbound NAT for package downloads.
- DNS: create controlplane.{customer-domain} A/AAAA records or internal CNAMEs for LB IPs. TTL low (30s) for first 24h during cutover.
- Certificates: have KMS/HSM keys or a CA chain available; annotate Terraform variable cert_root_pem when using customer-supplied certs.
- Inventory: GPU/node counts + instance types are provisioned (if onprem bare metal, check BMC access for PXE).
- Secrets: KMS access tested (kms:Encrypt/Decrypt), service principal with least privilege, and a passphrase-backed secrets seal.
- Monitoring: temporary Prometheus scrape targets and grafana links prepared for smoke dashboards.

BOOTSTRAP ORDER (idempotent sequence):
1) VPC & core infra (TF apply): subnets, route tables, security groups, NAT/egress, bastion (if required).
2) KMS & secrets store: create customer KMS key rings/policies, store initial seed key.
3) DNS records (placeholder IPs if using ephemeral LB).
4) Terraform: core control-plane infra modules (controlplane-network -> controlplane-iam -> controlplane-nodes).
5) Operator CRDs and image pull secrets: apply after nodes join.
6) Ingress/LB and certificate provisioning.
7) Smoke deploy a single replica controlplane service, run end-to-end sanity.
8) Bump to target replica count via autoscaler or TF-controlled ASG/VM group.

TF PRAGMATICS (patterns we've found reduce accidental drift):
- Keep short-lived resources (nodes, ephemeral LBs) in a separate 'worker' workspace from long-lived artifacts (kms, terraform state buckets).
- Use locals and versioned modules with explicit semantic versions (avoid git @master). Example: module "controlplane_core" { source = "git::https://.../modules/controlplane-core.git?ref=v1.12.0" }
- Parameterize security groups by intent ("management", "node-comm", "metrics") instead of opening by port numbers spread across modules.
- Explicit lifecycle ignore_changes on autoscaling/instance state fields that external autoscaler modifies: lifecycle { ignore_changes = ["desired_capacity"] } for the TF-managed group if the autoscaler adjusts it.
- Keep provider blocks explicit per workspace: provider "aws" { alias = "customer" region = var.region } and pass providers to modules to avoid accidental cross-customer reads.

SAMPLE TF SNIPPET (pragmatic bits you can copy):
resource "aws_autoscaling_group" "controlplane_nodes" {
  name = "cp-${var.customer_id}-nodes"
  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = ["desired_capacity"] # autoscaler owns desired_capacity at runtime
  }
  tag { key = "Name" value = "cp-${var.customer_id}" propagate_at_launch = true }
}

UPGRADE AND ROTATION PLAN (operator + nodes):
- Goal: perform an operator binary or module upgrade with minimal disruption and easily reversible actions.
- Strategy: staged rolling rotations with canary (1-2 instances) followed by bulk rolling with health gates and automatic pause points.

Step A — Canary (safest start):
1) Mark trunk image tag for canary (e.g., redwood/controlplane:2026.02-canary).
2) Scale a canary node pool to +2 replicas (taint other nodes to avoid scheduling if necessary).
3) Route 1–5% of traffic to the canary operator via smart routing (if available) or run synthetic traffic against it.
4) Monitor: request latency, error rate, KV store latencies, leader election churn in logs.
5) If telemetry ok for 15–30m, continue. If not, revert image tag and drain canary nodes.

Step B — Rolling rotation (bulk):
- Use a rolling update with maxUnavailable=1 (k8s) or batch size 1 for VM pools.
- For stateful components (etcd etc): always validate snapshot and backup before rolling.
- Drain sequence: cordon -> gracefully drain -> wait for all pod readiness to pass on replacement -> remove old instance.

Rollback triggers and commands (quick):
- If global error spike >5% above baseline sustained for 10m OR controlplane becomes >30s slower for 99th percentile:
  - Pause rotation: terraform apply to pin previous module version OR patch deployment image back to prior tag: kubectl set image deployment/controlplane controlplane=redwood/controlplane:prev-tag
  - Revert DNS if cutover changed endpoints (switch to blue LB).
  - Re-instate old KMS keys or secrets path if new keys caused decrypt failures.

SCALES & CAPACITY HEURISTICS:
- Small deployment: 3 control plane replicas, 2 worker nodes; aim for <200 rps sustained.
- Medium: 5–7 control plane replicas, autoscale pool 5–15 nodes.
- Large/Enterprise: dedicated HA etcd cluster (3–5 nodes), controlplane 7–11, worker fleet with zone spread.
- Batching tip: if tokenized workloads are high latency-per-token, increase request parallelism and use prefix caching. Monitor tokens/sec/gpu to judge batch targets.

SMOKE VALIDATION CHECKLIST (post-bootstrap / post-upgrade):
- API health endpoint returns 200 /healthz on all controlplane replicas.
- End-to-end request: create model session -> generate short text -> assert no decrypt errors.
- KV and caches: perform read/write sanity for prefixes used by SDK.
- Metrics: token generation p50/p99 within 1.5x baseline, errors <0.5% for core routes.
- Telemetry: traces sampled and appear in tracing system for new nodes.

QUICK COMMANDS (ops cheat sheet):
- Force rotate a single node (k8s): kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data && wait && kubectl uncordon <replacement>
- Repoint DNS temporarily: gcloud dns record-sets transaction start -> remove / add -> execute (or use customer's DNS API)
- Snapshot etcd: etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINTS} --cacert=...

POST-ROTATION VERIFICATION (10m, 1h, 24h checks):
- 10m: health endpoints, no crashloops, errors stable.
- 1h: latency SLOs affirmed, resource usage (cpu/mem/gpu) within expected ranges.
- 24h: any slow-degrading signals (GC, memory leaks) surface; hold an incident review if degradation observed.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (please update before handoff):
- Determine final naming convention for terraform workspaces per customer (workspace prefix vs per-account state). (owner: Miguel)
- Confirm backup cadence policy for etcd with customer compliance (Owner: Priya).
- Validate HSM integration steps (work with crypto team to produce succinct how-to). (owner: Ben)

RISK NOTES & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: drift between operator-managed desired_capacity and TF-managed desired_capacity. Mitigation: pick one owner (prefer autoscaler) and ignore_changes in TF for that attribute.
- Risk: certificate expiration during upgrade. Mitigation: preflight cert checks and automated renewal test as part of canary.
- Risk: network ACLs blocking scrape/health endpoints. Mitigation: temporary permissive egress rule for first 24h then lock down.

Appendix: useful links and snippets
- Example TF workspace split pattern: 1) core (kms, dns, iam), 2) infra (vpc, subnet, lb), 3) runtime (node pools, autoscaler).
- Example k8s rollout pause: kubectl rollout pause deployment/controlplane && kubectl rollout resume deployment/controlplane
- Slack channels: #private-deploys, #sre-oncall (ping sop@redwood for emergency)

If you take anything from this doc: copy the PRE-FLIGHT CHECKS and SMOKE VALIDATION CHECKLIST into the customer onboarding ticket and use them verbatim for the first install.
